Hi Alex,

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — great conversation and lots of alignment on where Redwood could fit into FastFleet's in-app assistant roadmap. I wanted to capture the follow-ups and a recommended path for the pilot so we can get you running on Hosted quickly while keeping Dedicated/Private options open if you need stricter isolation down the line.

Summary of what we heard from your side:
- Use case: contextual assistant for drivers + post-trip summarization for ops
- Expected profile: bursty traffic (peak ~50 rps for short windows), average ~120 tokens per request, some long-output generation for summaries (up to ~1k tokens occasionally)
- Data posture: need for SOC 2 compliance and audit logs; potential future need for VPC/on-prem for regulated customers

Recommended pilot (Hosted-first):
1) Start on Hosted API for a 4‑week functional pilot — fastest to validate latency and output quality.
2) Provision an evaluation quota scoped to your endpoints (chat + summarization) and a modest rate cap we can raise on demand.
3) Use streaming for the assistant flows and prefix caching for repetitive prompts to control cost.
4) If isolation/SLA needs show up, we can evaluate Dedicated capacity or a Private VPC rollout — same API semantics, different infra.

Next steps I need from you:
- Confirm whether the pilot can use Hosted in us-west1 (if you need EU residency, flag it now).
- Confirm initial target peak rps to provision a safe rate cap (I recommend starting at 100 rps to give headroom).
- Procurement contact to start paperwork (if you want an MSA/PO route for the pilot).

Attachments: I've attached a short Redwood quickstart checklist and a blank usage estimate CSV to capture your expected traffic pattern.

Proposed timeline:
- Quota & test keys: 1–2 business days after we have the usage numbers
- Pilot start: within the week after keys are provisioned

If that sounds good, I'll get the test keys and a small guide from Dev to configure streaming and recommended endpoints.

Best,

Alex — quick technical answers to the points you raised: 

- Per-endpoint rate limits: yes — Hosted supports route-level rate caps. We can configure different limits for /v1/chat and /v1/summarize and apply token-based guards. For the pilot we typically set conservative per-route caps and raise them after observing patterns.
- Long runs and token handling: Hosted supports up to 4k tokens on default models; you can stream incrementally to avoid hitting client-side timeouts. Summaries at ~1k tokens are expected and won't trigger throttles unless they run concurrently at scale.
- Data residency: Hosted stores logs and cached artifacts in the region where the tenant is provisioned. If you pick us-west1, EU data will not be mirrored there. For regulated EU-only workloads we recommend Private or Dedicated in an EU region.
- VPC peering: not available on the standard Hosted plane. VPC peering / private network ingress is available on Redwood Private (and some Dedicated configurations). If you think you'll need VPC peering for production, start that evaluation early — Dedicated lead time is ~2–4 weeks to provision reserved pools; Private (VPC/on-prem) is longer and requires security review.
- Suggested pilot config: Hosted in us-west1, per-route caps: assistant 100 rps, summarization 20 rps; token cap initial budget 500k tokens/day (we can dial this after week 1). Enable streaming and prefix caching for repetitive prompts.

I've attached a short ops note we hand to customers during pilots that includes recommended SDK settings and streaming examples.

If you share the filled usage CSV, I can propose a tighter quota and put an ops ticket in to pre-warm caches.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
